description:
The floating ball window's own boundary, one permission wide: it may start an operating-system drag of itself, and nothing else about any window.

**Why this is a second capability rather than a line in `desktop-pet.json`.** That file's windows are selected by `pet-*`, which the ball matches — it must, or it would hold no IPC at all — so anything added there is granted to the character windows as well. Its own description says the pet's windows 「may not move any window — including their own」, and that sentence is still true of the character window: it has no drag affordance and no page asks for one. Adding `start-dragging` there would widen a boundary for a consumer that does not exist. This file names one window (`pet-ball`, the label `desktop_pet/ball.rs` mints) and grants one permission, so the union a window receives is stated per surface: the ball can move itself, the character window cannot move anything.

`core:window:allow-start-dragging` is what `getWindowControls().startDragging()` needs (`platform/window.ts`), and it is the whole of what the ball's drag calls: the compositor owns the movement once it starts, so no position, geometry or monitor permission is granted, and §7.3's ban on per-frame IPC is satisfied by construction rather than by discipline. `snap` — the reference's other half, which parked the window against an edge and persisted the position — is deliberately not wired: it needs `allow-outer-position`, `allow-current-monitor` and `allow-set-position` (three more, for a window that nothing would remember the position of across a launch), and the port declares it optional so its absence is a state the orb states rather than a permission this file can afford.
